headline: インフォメーション is borrowed from English information.
Komoru is from Old Japanese 隠る (komoru), and its stem relates to “fill, filling”, so it is likely cognate with 込む (komu, “to be crowded, be packed”).
Shūgiin is 衆議 (shūgi, “general consultation, general conference”) plus 院 (-in, “parliamentary chamber”).
Jinkaku is said to be coined by Inoue Tetsujirō as a translation of English personality.
サイズ is from English size.
キャリア is from English career, though its pitch accent suggests English carrier.
ネガ is a shortening of ネガティブ (negatibu), from English negative.
Kokorogake is the nominative form of 心掛ける (kokorokakeru, “try, endeavor”).
In chōhen, 編 is a daiyōji replacing 篇.
パチンコ appears from the Taishō period, a compound of ぱちん (pachin, onomatopoeia for a small hard thing striking something else) plus 子 (-ko).
Miharashi is the continuative stem of the verb 見晴らす (miharasu, “to overlook, look out over”).
Sasageru is from Old Japanese 捧ぐ (sasagu), a contraction of 差し上ぐ (sasiagu), whence modern 差し上げる (sashiageru).
Dōteki is 動 (dō) plus 的 (-teki).
Nagisa is from Old Japanese, possibly 凪ぎ (nagi, “calming, dying down”) plus 磯 (sa, “rocky shore, pebble beach”).
In muchi, 知 is a daiyōji replacing 智.
Hikan is from the Buddhist Middle Chinese term 悲觀 (“compassionate view”), later reanalyzed as 悲 (“sadness”) plus 観 (“outlook”).
Bi, “beauty”, is from Middle Chinese 美 (MC mijX).
Oshikiru is 押し (oshi, the stem of 押す (osu)) plus 切る (kiru, “to cut”).
Sekkai is 切 (setsu, “cut”) plus 開 (kai, “open”).
Shinjitsu is from Middle Chinese 真實 (MC tsyin zyit).
Onaidoshi is an alteration of 同じ年.
Kurōto is 玄 (kuro, “deep, profound”) plus 人 (-uto, “person”), an old root form of 人 (hito).
Shiyōnin is 使用 (shiyō) plus 人 (-nin).
Onbu is from おぶう (obuu).
Hyotto has an onomatopoeic ひょ (hyo) element, plus と (to), an adverb-forming particle.
レギュラー is from English regular.
チェンジ is borrowed from English change.
Nukedasu is 抜け (nuke, the stem of 抜ける (nukeru, “to be extracted, to come out”)) plus 出す (dasu, “to take out”).
Taimen is from the Middle Chinese compound 對面 (MC twojH mjienH).
Nebiki is 値 (ne, “price”) plus 引き (hiki, “reducing”), with hiki voiced to biki by rendaku.
Tonda is the past or perfective of 飛ぶ (tobu, “to deviate from common sense”), and is unrelated to とんでもない (tondemonai, “outrageous”).
